subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity — recap and priorities

Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on priorities and blockers:

• Goals: move critical inference workloads (patient summarization, triage bot) off our experimental clusters to a dedicated, SLA-backed environment by Q3. Primary goals are predictable latency (p95 target ~250–300ms for 1k concurrent sessions), data isolation, and simplified admin controls for compliance audits.

• Capacity ask: reserve ~4x A100-equivalent GPUs to start with a defined scaling policy (scale to 8 GPUs during peak) — estimating ~2M tokens/day initially. We’ll need predictable throughput and a way to pin model versions.

• Isolation & security: VPC peering or private endpoint is required; SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration for key management will be assessed by our security team.

• SLAs: looking for 99.9% uptime for core inference endpoints and a latency SLO at p95; we’re open to discussion on credits/exceptions tied to scheduled maintenance windows.

• Next steps: please send a short architecture sketch, proposed scaling policy, and an estimated monthly cost range. I attached our initial requirements spreadsheet for context.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Matthews | Head of AI Platforms
Aurora Health

Jordan — great to meet you and Asha today. Appreciate the clear priorities; confirming back the points and our proposed next steps below.

Recap/pain points (we heard):
- Predictable p95 latency target ~250–300ms for ~1k concurrent sessions
- Data isolation: VPC/private endpoints + KMS/HSM for keys
- Reserved GPUs with burst capacity and a clear scaling plan
- SOC 2 / audit artifacts required by security/compliance

What we’ll deliver by EOD Tue (3 business days):
1) Architecture sketch for a Dedicated deployment showing VPC peering, private endpoints, and KMS flow.
2) Suggested reserved capacity plan: start with 4x reserved A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscale policy to 8 GPUs at 70% CPU/Util threshold, and a burst policy for daily peak windows.
3) Draft SLA terms and example credit schedule for outages/maintenance.
4) Ballpark pricing range and a 30/60/90 day ramp plan tied to usage.

Internal asks (cc’d): Dylan — can you prepare the scaling/cost estimates and a short runbook for failure scenarios? Neha — please pull our SOC 2 artifact pack and a short explanation of KMS integration options to share with Aurora’s security team.

Next meeting: Jordan, I’ve shared a booking link for an SE deep dive next Wed/Thu (link below). If those times don’t work, propose alternatives.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 11:00 AM PDT Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dylan — can you prepare the scaling/cost estimates and a short runbook for failure scenarios?

Working on it — initial notes below so we can sync before sending to Aurora: 

• Capacity baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (we recommend ML-accelerated A100-40 configuration) supports ~900–1,100 concurrent short-context sessions with our batching and KV cache.
• Autoscale: trigger scale-out at 70% sustained utilization over 10 min; scale-in after 15 min below 50%. Recommend soft limit to 8 GPUs with on-demand burst to 12 for short peaks (billing at on-demand rate).
• Latency SLO: with 4 GPUs we project p95 ~260ms for 1k concurrent sessions (text-generation w/ 1.5k token avg). We’ll include profiling numbers and a small test harness.
• Failure runbook (short): fallback routing to hosted-compatible model variants, per-request retries with jitter, and degraded-mode token caps to protect latency SLOs.

I’ll assemble the cost model (reserved vs committed monthly pricing + burst rates) and a short HA/runbook doc. Marissa — do you want me to include a sample canary rollout plan (A/B routing by percentage) for model upgrades?

—Dylan
